sparse-graph.why: The matrix needs 10¹⁰ cells, almost all empty. An adjacency list stores only the roads that exist and lists a place's neighbours directly. An edge list is compact but needs a full scan to find neighbours.

matrix-edge-check.why: It's a single array lookup, matrix[u][v]. That speed is what the matrix's O(V²) memory buys.

list-space.why: One list per vertex, plus one entry per edge (two for an undirected edge).

build-list.why: Each undirected edge is added in both directions, so vertex 0 lists 1 and 2, vertex 2 lists 0 and 3, and so on.

directed-undirected.why: An undirected edge u–v is stored in u's list and in v's list, so you can walk it from either end.
